says: In today's tooling, the law file 'T1074 a local typecheck waits for the lock and any running compiler' starts a stand-in compiler in named() and polls pgrep -x for it every 20 ms up to a 5 s wall clock. On a loaded CI runner node's start can pass 5 s, or pgrep can look before the stand-in has written its name back on Linux, so the law fails with 'the stand-in compiler never started' on code that cannot reach it.
proof: CI run 43831921638, leg tests (tooling-2), at eeb8ecdbb: 'AssertionError: the stand-in compiler never started: expected false to be true'. The same law was green on that branch's earlier run 43823291196 and on main's full run 43820371869, and the branch does not touch scripts/typecheck*.
cost: Any pull request whose CI runs the tooling legs can go red for no fault of its own, and a person must rerun it and compare against main to tell.
